overview: Create the shared controls and result containers. No intensity is calculated in this cell. All three models retain the material, orientation and optical choices.

blocks.title: Model and polarization controls
blocks.explanation: Create the three model choices and the VV/VH/σ⁺α selector.
blocks.why: Material and polarization are independent inputs.
blocks.check: The redundant example selector is not displayed in the application.

blocks.title: Material and complex tensor inputs
blocks.explanation: Create material, point-group, mode and coefficient inputs with short definitions.
blocks.why: A coefficient size and phase specify its complex value.
blocks.check: Si and GaAs are separate cubic entries and all models show the same list.

blocks.title: Surface, lattice and frame preview
blocks.explanation: Create hkl, uvw, normal side, ψ, lattice and manual-T inputs, plus the frame preview output.
blocks.why: X, Y, Z and T must be available before an intensity scan.
blocks.check: An invalid in-plane direction or frame is reported instead of silently changed.

blocks.title: Optical and display controls
blocks.explanation: Create the Jones-state preview and the display/export controls. Source-reference widgets remain internal to their separate original notebook workflow.
blocks.why: Only active selected values should enter the public crystal calculation.
blocks.check: Every public model offers the same three optical methods.

blocks.title: Result containers
blocks.explanation: Create mathematical, plot, frame, validation and export views.
blocks.why: A result and its input record must remain linked.
blocks.check: The explained view places definitions on the left and mathematics on the right.

pitfalls: The defaults are demonstrations; symmetry does not determine numerical tensor magnitudes or phases.
The circular OAM controls diagnose a conditional selection rule and do not implement a spatial vortex-light propagation calculation.
A fixed circular channel can appear as a circle in a polar display because its scalar intensity is independent of the displayed scan angle.

overview: Keep dependent widgets synchronized and update the measurement frame without an intensity calculation. Model changes preserve the chosen physical inputs.
workflow: X, Y, Z and T before intensity

blocks.title: Coefficient and material callbacks
blocks.explanation: Update mode values, optional Ag relations and material definitions.
blocks.why: A copied coefficient relation includes both size and phase.
blocks.check: Changing a coefficient invalidates the previous intensity result.

blocks.title: Geometry controls
blocks.explanation: Update surface presets or custom hkl and automatic/manual X references.
blocks.why: The in-plane direction must satisfy the zone condition.
blocks.check: A changed input leaves previous results marked as stale.

blocks.title: Actual polarization preview
blocks.explanation: Show the selected incident column, conjugated detection row and scan angle.
blocks.why: The optical method must be identified by its actual states.
blocks.check: VV/VH scan θ; σ⁺α scans α with the source phase convention.

blocks.title: X, Y, Z and T before intensity
blocks.explanation: Construct and display the current axes and T directly from orientation/lattice inputs.
blocks.why: The frame should be checked before running a long intensity calculation.
blocks.check: The preview contains no intensity or polar scan.

blocks.title: Load visible configuration values
blocks.explanation: Populate the shared controls and keep all three model routes available.
blocks.why: A report label is not an optical method.
blocks.check: All models keep orientation controls visible and all material choices available.

pitfalls: A form transaction prevents intermediate callbacks; it does not run the physics.
Changing a material preserves the selected orientation and optics, but updates illustrative tensor and lattice defaults that must be reviewed.
The active-profile guard is a regression safeguard: hidden circular-rule fields are ignored for noncircular optics, while active circular profiles still require a valid integer charge list.

overview: Read visible inputs, calculate once, then display and export that same result. Review inputs is a separate preparation action.

blocks.title: Collect inputs
blocks.explanation: Read the material, coefficients, lattice, hkl/uvw or manual T, normal side, ψ and optical method.
blocks.why: A calculation must use the values currently visible in the controls.
blocks.check: Inactive manual-T text is not parsed when hkl mode is selected.

blocks.title: Calculate and display
blocks.explanation: Prepare the frame and tensors, calculate curves and create the connected mathematical trace and figures.
blocks.why: The plots and equations must describe the same configuration.
blocks.check: A failed calculation reports the input error rather than exporting a stale result.

blocks.title: Export, validation and comparisons
blocks.explanation: Save the equations, data and figures, run reference checks and store comparison snapshots.
blocks.why: A saved comparison must retain its original inputs.
blocks.check: Keep raw CSV separate from display normalization.

blocks.title: Explain the equations
blocks.explanation: Render a numbered explanation and definitions beside each mathematical block.
blocks.why: Matrix substitutions and conjugate products should be readable without jumping to a distant legend.
blocks.check: Analytical tensor and intensity equations are red; the surrounding prose stays neutral.

blocks.title: Review before intensity
blocks.explanation: Display X/Y/Z, T, frame checks, transformed tensors and Jones states using preparation only.
blocks.why: This allows a user to inspect the setup before an intensity scan.
blocks.check: Review must not replace an already calculated result or run a new scan.

pitfalls: on_run() performs the calculation; on_export() packages the already stored calculation.
A closed Matplotlib registry handle does not destroy a figure object retained in state for later savefig export.
An individual Ag Cartesian contribution is not a separate phonon mode, and its power must not be read as the full coherent Ag response.

overview: Define independent scientific regression checks for tensor symmetry, the imported optical chain, crystal rotation, reference component laws, unresolved phonon components and numerical edge cases.
workflow: Construct point-group generators in the same Cartesian setting as the library.
Check tensor-subspace covariance, dimensions and selected irrep characters.
Compare optical and crystal calculations against independent matrix chains and analytic limits.
Exercise input rejection, zero signals, overflow and caller immutability.
Provide a single function that invokes the complete core/model regression set.

Run unchanged. This defines the core test functions; the completion message confirms their definitions loaded. To execute the actual checks, finish Cell 22 or press tool 8. Inspect Validation for PASS/failure evidence.

blocks.title: Construct generators in the library Cartesian convention
blocks.explanation: Rz creates a rotation about z; inv is inversion; the diagonal matrices give twofold rotations or mirrors. c3, c4 and c6 set principal rotational generators, while cycle permutes the cubic Cartesian axes. The dictionary selects the required generators for each of the 21 groups.
blocks.why: Tensor covariance is meaningful only when generator axes and tensor axes use the same setting. A C2 axis along y must not be tested as though it were along z.
blocks.check: These matrices operate on tensor coordinates in tests; improper symmetry operations are allowed as crystal symmetries even though an orientation frame itself must have determinant +1.

blocks.title: Test complete symmetric tensor subspaces and irrep labels
blocks.explanation: Complex trial coefficients exercise all allowed entries. Each tensor must be symmetric and 3-by-3. Under every generator, transformed component tensors are expressed in the original component span using least squares; reconstruction and component-mixing unitarity are checked. Selected representation traces are compared with expected characters. Coefficient derivatives from all families must span the six-dimensional space of symmetric second-rank tensors.
blocks.why: Matrix shape alone cannot detect a mislabeled irrep, wrong off-diagonal sign or incomplete family. Covariance tests the transformation rule, while character traces distinguish representations.
blocks.check: The test reports its covariance and character counts. It validates the declared symmetric electric-dipole library, not arbitrary magnetic or nonsymmetric response tensors.

blocks.title: Reproduce the original QWP matrix chain independently
blocks.explanation: Check the explicit Q matrix, Q.H*Q=I, Q_return=Q.T and the circular incident state. For several complex source parameters, embed the effective 2D model only for regression and compare the engine curve with a closed circular-basis formula at irregular angles.
blocks.why: A source regression should verify the phase, analyzer zero and matrix order rather than only show a visually similar polar curve. Irregular samples expose accidental agreement at special angles.
blocks.check: The 2D embedding in this test is an algebraic device; it is not a proposed symmetry tensor for CaNb2O6.

blocks.title: Prevent reference policies from leaking into the source or crystal routes
blocks.explanation: Verify that the original source has no crystal geometry or exported hkl, and that its amplitude and return phase match its circular derivation. Exercise source special cases. Compare the preserved historical component prescription and the coherent complete tensor against independent contractions, then change a relative phase to show their different interference rules. Invalid hybrid configurations must raise. Finally temporarily replace foreign crystal/reference helpers with functions that fail, run the pure source route and restore the globals in finally.
blocks.why: A calculation cannot be called a source reproduction if it silently imports another method’s tensor split or optical chain. The forbidden-call tests prove separation of execution paths rather than merely comparing final numbers.
blocks.check: The preserved historical component-power sum is a regression target; the new main Ag figures remain separate xx/yy/zz contributions.

blocks.title: Compare projection with an independent full 3D contraction
blocks.explanation: Use a reproducible complex random tensor on three surfaces with a noncubic metric and nonzero frame angle. For three optical chains and five angles, NumPy contracts the embedded incident/detection vectors with the full rotated tensor independently of the reduced calculation. Also test det(T)=+1 and invariance of an isotropic tensor.
blocks.why: The 2-by-2 optical projection must be justified by equality with the 3D field calculation, especially on tilted surfaces where crystal-z entries can project into the transverse plane.
blocks.check: There are 45 direct comparisons. Isotropic invariance applies to the complete coherent tensor, not to a basis-dependent sum of its component powers.

blocks.title: Check slide algebra without using it to generate curves
blocks.explanation: Build the reference frame and calculate three diagonal component tensors using arbitrary incident/detector phases. Compare against independently written overlap-factor laws, then check five coefficient choices in the specialized reference scan. Verify the denominator 144 and the symbolic expansion identity. Replace the closed reference helper with a function that raises and confirm the production matrix calculation still succeeds.
blocks.why: A reference law should test the program rather than supply the answer being tested. The forbidden-reference call directly guards against pasting a target formula into the production path.
blocks.check: The historical aggregate reference is retained here to verify earlier arrays; the general display policy is checked separately in Cell 21.

blocks.title: Test phonon-basis invariance and optical limiting cases
blocks.explanation: Randomly orthogonally mix the Eg, E2g and T2g component tensors and verify that their unresolved summed powers remain unchanged. Compare silicon’s direct-linear constant response with its different QWP sin-squared response. Verify basal-plane E1g extinction.
blocks.why: Orthogonal unresolved phonon components require a power sum that is invariant under a change of component basis. Different optical chains should retain their genuinely different limits.
blocks.check: Partner mixing is not the same operation as separating xx, yy and zz entries of one Ag phonon.

blocks.title: Reject invalid input and handle exact numerical limits
blocks.explanation: Serialize the caller configuration before and after calculation to test immutability. A zero tensor must produce a zero curve with no preferred angle. Invalid in-plane indices, a reflected frame and overflowing amplitudes must raise. Fixed optical profiles must discard inactive direct controls and export their actual parameters.
blocks.why: A trustworthy result includes correct failure behavior and input provenance, not just a valid-looking curve for the default case.
blocks.check: An exact zero has no unique maximum direction; a reflection must not be relabeled as a physical orientation rotation.

blocks.title: Run the core and reference-model checks in one call
blocks.explanation: The return list calls each named validation function and gathers its human-readable result. It also invokes the additional linear, circular, resonance and interference checks defined in Cell 21.
blocks.why: A single entry point lets startup, a notebook button or another interface execute the same scientific regressions. Function lookup occurs at call time, so Cell 21 must have run before this is invoked.
blocks.check: Any raised assertion stops the suite. Reaching the returned list means each listed check completed successfully.

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.
blocks.check: Run Cells 1–20 in order and confirm the Cell 20/22 message. Model/source checks must be inspected separately in Validation.

pitfalls: A preserved historical reference prescription is tested as a reference, not silently applied to the new general Ag plots.
Symmetry operations can have determinant -1; a measurement orientation frame must still have determinant +1.
Passing a finite test suite is evidence of algebraic consistency within scope, not a proof of every experimental effect or all crystallographic point groups.

overview: Define independent checks. The active public-model suite is at the end of the cell; original-source checks remain available for their source records.

blocks.title: Reference and edge-case checks
blocks.explanation: Retain checks of complex amplitudes, symmetry, extrema, interference and source formulas.
blocks.why: A plotted shape alone does not establish the correctness of the contraction.
blocks.check: Compare exact equations or independently calculated matrix products.

blocks.title: Document the checking procedures
blocks.explanation: Give each source check a purpose, independent expected result and numerical tolerance.
blocks.why: A pass statement needs recorded evidence and scope.
blocks.check: Source checks do not constitute a colleague or experimental review.

blocks.title: New-san analytical comparison
blocks.explanation: Compare paper-reference expressions and the program’s matrix response.
blocks.why: Reference formulas are tests, not fitted curves supplied to the engine.
blocks.check: Record any disagreement with a printed source expression explicitly.

blocks.title: Three-model checks
blocks.explanation: Check all retained Si/GaAs surfaces, three polarizations and three model routes against independent NumPy contractions. Test shared noncubic controls and preflight.
blocks.why: A model change must preserve geometry and polarization; the first-run example must be reproducible.
blocks.check: All model routes retain the full input controls and agree for identical physical inputs.

blocks.title: Shared optical choices
blocks.explanation: Check the model order, three methods per model and normalized Jones states.
blocks.why: The interface and mathematical definitions must agree.
blocks.check: The first selector reads Model 1 — New-san, Model 2 — My PPT slide, Model 3 — Dr. Kumar.

pitfalls: A necessary angular-momentum congruence is not sufficient to determine an intensity.
The general point-group loop uses conventional principal settings; the separate random full-3D test exercises tilted geometry.
A global complex phase cancels from intensity, while relative phases can change interference.
Native Origin execution is not verified by compiling its generated Python script.

overview: Open the application, run the supplied Silicon (500) example and execute the validation procedures. No code edits are needed for the first run.

blocks.title: Short starting instructions
blocks.explanation: Explain the goal and the numbered path from inputs to exported results.
blocks.why: A newcomer should be able to run the supplied case first.
blocks.check: Silicon (500), T₂g, d=1, VV is the initial example.

blocks.title: Material and orientation panels
blocks.explanation: Assemble shared material, lattice, hkl/uvw, manual-frame and Jones-state controls.
blocks.why: The model choice must not hide the axes or remove the lattice controls.
blocks.check: The frame preview is available before intensity.

blocks.title: Application layout
blocks.explanation: Place model and polarization first, then inputs, review, calculate and result views.
blocks.why: A separate Example/Load pair would duplicate the first-run setup.
blocks.check: The optional user guidance does not change physical inputs.

blocks.title: Callbacks and checked starting result
blocks.explanation: Connect controls once, load Si (500), calculate its polar plot and run the checks.
blocks.why: The success messages and evidence come from an executed starting case.
blocks.check: VV must match sin²(2θ) with d=1; the printed revision must match the download.

pitfalls: Run Cells 1–21 before this cell; a fresh kernel and Run All rebuilds edited definitions.
The T2g curve sums the intensities of three orthogonal phonon components; d=1 is a relative coefficient scale.
The initial notebook and website both use Silicon (500), VV; the other material examples remain selectable.
